Released: 3 November 2026

Version 2.3.0 stops holding the valid `spec.scenarios` values in the operator, so a scenario a Hybrid Manager (HM) version adds installs without an operator upgrade; refuses to uninstall an installed scenario unless you confirm it; redeploys a settled installation periodically so that resources deleted outside the operator are recreated; and stops copying image pull secrets into every namespace in the cluster.

## Highlights

- **The values `spec.scenarios` accepts now come from the HM version you install, not from the operator.** The operator reads them from the `scenarios.json` of the version in `spec.version` instead of a list fixed in its CRD and admission webhook, so a scenario a later HM version adds needs no operator upgrade. A well-formed name the target version doesn't define is admitted and then dropped from the spec with an event, where earlier versions rejected it outright.

- **Image pull secrets are no longer copied to every namespace in the cluster.** The operator stops adding `replicator.v1.mittwald.de/replicate-to: "*"` to the secrets named in `spec.registry.imagePullSecrets`, so a secret reaches only the namespaces its own replicator annotations name. `edbctl` 1.11 or later annotates the pull secret it creates. If you create the secret by hand, annotate it yourself, or workloads outside its namespace can't pull their images. An existing installation is unaffected: upgrading the operator doesn't remove an annotation an earlier version added.

- **Removing an installed scenario from `spec.scenarios` is refused unless you confirm it with an annotation.** Re-applying a manifest that lists fewer scenarios than are installed now fails at admission instead of uninstalling those components and losing the data they hold. Pipelines that re-apply a trimmed manifest need the confirmation annotation.

- **A settled installation is redeployed every hour so that resources deleted outside the operator come back.** Only missing resources are recreated; a resource that was edited rather than deleted is left alone. Set `--component-drift-interval` on the manager to change the interval, or to a negative duration to turn the pass off.

## Features

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><details><summary>Resources deleted outside the operator are recreated automatically
</summary><p>A settled installation is now redeployed once an hour so that <code>kapp</code> recreates any resource of a component that was deleted outside the operator. Until now the operator decided whether to deploy a component by comparing the hash of its rendered manifests with the hash in <code>status.components[]</code>, and that comparison matched whether or not the resources it describes still existed, so a component deleted by hand stayed missing indefinitely. Only creates are applied — a resource that was edited rather than deleted is left alone — and the operator records a <code>Drifted</code> warning event naming the component whose resources it put back, or a <code>DriftCheckFailed</code> warning when the redeploy itself couldn't run. Pass <code>--component-drift-interval</code> to the manager through <code>controllerManager.manager.args</code> in the operator Helm chart to change the interval; a negative duration turns the pass off.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>The scenarios the operator settled on are reported in <code>status.scenarios</code>
</summary><p><code>status.scenarios</code> records what the operator resolved for the version it last settled: the <code>version</code> it resolved against, the scenario names that version <code>defined</code>, the <code>dependencies</code> between them, and the <code>installed</code> set it deployed. Read it with <code>kubectl get hybridcontrolplane edbpgai -o yaml</code> to see which scenarios are installed and which names the target version knows, instead of inferring both from <code>spec.scenarios</code>.</p>
</details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>


## Enhancements

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><details><summary>Tunable CPU and memory for the automated upgrade jobs
</summary><p>You can now size the container of the jobs the operator runs during an HM upgrade with the <code>upgrade_job_cpu_request</code>, <code>upgrade_job_cpu_limit</code>, <code>upgrade_job_memory_request</code>, and <code>upgrade_job_memory_limit</code> global parameters. They default to <code>50m</code> and <code>1</code> for CPU and to <code>128Mi</code> and <code>1Gi</code> for memory, and when you set one half of a pair past the other's default, that default follows it — a request above the default limit raises the limit, a limit below the default request lowers the request. A value that isn't a Kubernetes quantity greater than zero, or a request above the limit you set for it, is rejected at admission.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>The <code>edb-object-storage</code> secret can live in <code>edb-system</code>
</summary><p>The operator reads the default object storage credentials from the <code>edb-object-storage</code> secret in either the <code>default</code> or the <code>edb-system</code> namespace, instead of <code>default</code> alone, so an installation that keeps platform secrets out of <code>default</code> can hold it with the rest of them. Keep exactly one copy: preflight reports the default object storage as <code>Invalid</code> when the secret exists in both namespaces.</p>
</details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>


## Changes

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><details><summary>The scenario names <code>spec.scenarios</code> accepts come from the target Hybrid Manager version
</summary><p>The names you can list in <code>spec.scenarios</code> are the ones defined by the <code>scenarios.json</code> of the Hybrid Manager version in <code>spec.version</code>, rather than a fixed list in the operator's CRD and admission webhook. A name made of lowercase letters, digits, and <code>-</code>, up to 63 characters, is admitted even when the target version doesn't define it; the operator then removes it from <code>spec.scenarios</code> and records a <code>ScenariosDropped</code> event, so a version that retires a scenario stops installing and reporting it while earlier versions keep it. A name that isn't well formed, such as the legacy <code>monitoringLogging</code>, is still stripped by the defaulting webhook, so a manifest carrying one keeps applying as before. Upgrading the operator leaves an existing <code>spec.scenarios</code> as it is, and <code>core</code> is still always installed.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Removing an installed scenario has to be confirmed
</summary><p>An update that drops a scenario the installation is running from <code>spec.scenarios</code> is rejected, because applying it uninstalls that scenario's components along with the data they hold. The error names the command that confirms the removal — <code>kubectl annotate hybridcontrolplanes.edbpgai.edb.com edbpgai edbpgai.edb.com/confirm-scenario-removal=&lt;names&gt; --overwrite</code> — after which you repeat your change; the operator clears the annotation once the new set has settled, so a confirmation doesn't carry over to a later edit. A scenario that another listed scenario depends on isn't treated as removed, because the operator adds it back. If the admission webhook is bypassed, the reconciler stops instead of uninstalling anything, setting the <code>ScenarioRemovalBlocked</code> condition and recording a warning event with the same instruction.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Image pull secrets are no longer replicated to every namespace
</summary><p><strong>Action required for a pull secret you create by hand.</strong> The operator no longer stamps <code>replicator.v1.mittwald.de/replicate-to: &quot;*&quot;</code> on the secrets named in <code>spec.registry.imagePullSecrets</code> (or the deprecated <code>spec.imagePullSecrets</code>), which copied the registry credentials into every namespace in the cluster, project namespaces included. Distributing the secret is now left to whatever created it: <code>edbctl</code> 1.11 or later annotates the pull secret it creates with the namespaces that pull with it. If you create the secret by hand, annotate it with <code>replicator.v1.mittwald.de/replicate-to</code> or <code>replicator.v1.mittwald.de/replicate-to-matching</code> for those namespaces yourself. Upgrading the operator doesn't remove an annotation an earlier version added, so the pull secret of an existing installation keeps being copied as before. The operator logs a message naming the secret when it finds no replicator annotation on it, and still fails the reconcile when a configured pull secret doesn't exist at all.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>One <code>HybridControlPlane</code> per cluster, named <code>edbpgai</code>
</summary><p>Creating a <code>HybridControlPlane</code> under any name other than <code>edbpgai</code>, or creating a second one in a cluster that already holds one, is rejected at admission. The beacon, <code>edbctl</code>, and the bootstrap and upgrade tooling all address the installation by that name, and a second resource stops reconciliation on both. The rule is enforced on create only, so an existing installation under another name keeps reconciling: it draws an admission warning on every update and a <code>NonStandardName</code> warning event from the reconciler, and reinstalling as <code>edbpgai</code> is what clears it.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>An initial installation fails preflight when its object storage folder isn't empty
</summary><p>A first installation whose <code>spec.globalParameters.internal_backup_folder</code> already holds objects — anything an earlier Hybrid Manager left in the bucket, not just its database backups — is now refused by preflight instead of installing on top of them. <code>kubectl get preflight -o yaml</code> reports it under <code>status.initializationChecks</code>, naming the folder and how many objects are in it. Empty the folder, or set <code>internal_backup_folder</code> to an unused 12-character value, as a new installation requires.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary><code>beacon_server_replicas</code> is validated
</summary><p>The <code>beacon_server_replicas</code> parameter of the <code>upm-beacon</code> component must be <code>0</code> or <code>1</code> where it is set, because the beacon server isn't built to run more than one replica. An update that changes it to anything else is rejected, while an installation that already carries another value and leaves it alone gets an admission warning instead, so it keeps reconciling.</p>
</details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>


## Bug Fixes

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><details><summary>The operator could crash while streaming a component's deploy output
</summary><p>Fixed a bug where the buffer that turns <code>kapp</code>'s output into per-component log lines was appended to from several goroutines during a single deploy, which corrupted it and could crash the manager mid-install. The writer is now locked, so the output of a component that reports on many resource types at once stays intact and attributable to it.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>A component whose version changed but whose manifests didn't kept reporting its old version
</summary><p>Fixed a bug where <code>status.components[].version</code> was rewritten only when a component's manifest hash or state changed, so a component that a new Hybrid Manager version ships unchanged went on reporting the version it was first installed at. The status now records the version a component was last deployed at, which is what <code>edbctl hybrid-manager status</code> and <code>kubectl describe hybridcontrolplane</code> show.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Informers logged errors for custom resource definitions that had been removed
</summary><p>Fixed a bug where removing a custom resource definition the operator watches — uninstalling Hybrid Manager removes SPIRE's, for example — left its informer retrying, with every retry logged at error level with a stack trace until the operator restarted. A watched type that is no longer served is now reported once at info level and after that at verbosity 4, and logged again when it is served once more.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>A suspended component is no longer rendered
</summary><p>A component suspended with <code>edbctl hybrid-manager suspend-component</code> is now skipped before its charts are rendered, rather than being rendered and then held, and its existing entry in <code>status.components[]</code> is carried forward unchanged. Resuming it with <code>edbctl hybrid-manager resume-component</code> deploys it as before.</p>
</details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>
